20. On meticulous examination the materials on record, it appears that the Opposite Party Nos. 2 and 3 admittedly purchased all shares of the BSTC Shipping Ltd. on 10-10-2011 and converted it into under name and style of JAC Shipping and Logistics Ltd. and still they are continuing the business. Since the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 are in the management of the company and naturally at the time of the purchase they had received all the documents including vedor agreement from the accused Nos. 3 to 7 and  it is clearly evident from the object clause of the Company. In such paradigm, presumption would  be that the Opposite Party Nos. 2 and 3 are in  possession of the Vendor Agreement. 

 21. It is very interesting that opposite Nos. 2 and 3 have not taken any stand that they do not possess the Vendor Agreement and besides that they have not taken any stand that the Vendor Agreement has been lost in the meantime. In such  backdrop the conclusive presumption may be drawn that the Vendor Agreement is within the possession of the company's present owner and in such attending facts the next question posed as to whether they can be summoned under section 94 of the Code to produce the vendor agreement.
